paper_metadata.title: Classical and quantum computing methods for estimating loan-level risk distributions

experiments.description: Theoretical quantum Monte Carlo / quantum amplitude estimation setup for estimating the 95th percentile of lifetime probability of default under an unconditional PD model, using N time-step distributions loaded into m-qubit registers and summed into a lifetime PD estimate.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Monte Carlo with Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) for unconditional lifetime PD

hyperparameters.distribution_type: logit-normal approximated by lognormal/normal in logit space

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each forecast-horizon unconditional PD distribution UPD(t) is loaded into an m-qubit register; N such registers are summed to form a lifetime PD estimate. The threshold test qubit C marks whether the sum exceeds x.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the cumulative probability / quantile x(a) of the lifetime PD distribution, where a is the probability that the lifetime loss is below threshold x.

problem_instance.description: Freddie Mac mortgage data, 30-year fixed-rate conforming mortgages; simplified quantum case uses unconditional probability of default at each forecast horizon rather than competing risks.
problem_instance.dataset_size: More than $2 trillion of conforming mortgages in the source data; four example loans used for classical illustration

dataset_specification.description: 30-year fixed-rate conforming mortgages; account-level variables include balance, delinquency status, payments, pay-off, origination date, origination score, postal code, LTV, DTI, number of borrowers, property type, and loan purpose. Forecast horizon in the paper is 36 months for the example accounts.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: APC decomposition used to estimate lifecycle and environment; multihorizon survival model with fixed lifecycle/environment inputs; unconditional PD redefined as DefaultAccounts(t)/BookedAccounts(t=0); logit-normal distributions approximated by lognormal distributions for loading into quantum registers.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: The paper provides a theoretical mapping to QAE and compares asymptotic sample complexity to classical Monte Carlo; no actual quantum hardware evaluation.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: APC decomposition; panel logistic regression for horizon-specific coefficients; Ornstein-Uhlenbeck extrapolation of environment; fit lognormal distribution to Monte Carlo outputs.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Quantum algorithm would use QAE and bisection search over threshold x to recover the desired quantile; classical baseline uses Monte Carlo tabulation and distribution fitting.

speedup_claims.conditions: for quantum amplitude estimation (QAE) when estimating the 95th percentile / cumulative probability threshold
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the asymptotic QAE error scales as O(1/M) versus classical Monte Carlo O(1/sqrt(M)); this is a theoretical sample-complexity claim, not a hardware demonstration.

speedup_claims.factor: tens of simulations instead of thousands
speedup_claims.conditions: when the final lifetime PD distribution is known to be well-approximated by a lognormal distribution
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a classical shortcut enabled by distributional fitting, not a quantum speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/M) estimation error for QAE; sample complexity improves as O(sqrt(M)) relative to classical Monte Carlo

experiments.description: Theoretical quantum Monte Carlo / quantum amplitude estimation setup for the full competing-risks lifetime PD calculation, where conditional default and attrition probabilities are propagated through survival S(t) and UPD(t)=CPD(t)·S(t).

algorithm.variant: Quantum Monte Carlo with QAE for competing-risks conditional PD/PA lifetime distribution

problem_formulation.encoding_details: At each time step, two new registers are loaded for CPD(t) and CPA(t), plus an entangled copy of CPD(t); a register for S(t) is also maintained and copied in entangled form for use in S(t+1).
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the lifetime default probability under competing risks: S(t)=S(t-1)·(1-CPD(t-1)-CPA(t-1)), UPD(t)=CPD(t)·S(t), then aggregate over time.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Entanglement via controlled gates (e.g., CNOT) is required so that the same sampled CPD(t) can be reused consistently in both UPD(t) and S(t+1).

problem_instance.description: Freddie Mac mortgage competing-risks model with conditional default and attrition probabilities across forecast horizons; intended for a five-year auto-loan-style scaling example in the discussion.
problem_instance.dataset_size: Freddie Mac mortgage portfolio; four example loans used for classical simulation illustration

dataset_specification.description: Competing-risks setup with conditional PD and PA estimated from multihorizon survival models; forecast horizon examples include 36 months and horizon-specific panel logistic regressions for h in [1,12].

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: APC decomposition for lifecycle and environment; horizon-specific panel logistic regressions for PD and PA; Ornstein-Uhlenbeck extrapolation of environment; Monte Carlo sampling from prediction intervals.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: The paper is a feasibility analysis only; no quantum hardware run. Resource scaling is argued analytically, including a five-year auto loan example.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical competing-risks survival model estimation; horizon-specific logistic regressions; OU extrapolation; Monte Carlo baseline.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Theoretical QAE would estimate the quantile of the lifetime loss distribution; bisection search over threshold x is described.

speedup_claims.conditions: for QAE applied to the competing-risks lifetime PD calculation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper argues the same QAE sample-complexity improvement applies in principle, but the full competing-risks formulation requires many registers and is not feasible on near-term hardware.

speedup_claims.factor: not feasible in the next couple years
speedup_claims.conditions: for a five-year auto loan example with m=8 and N forecast steps
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the best-case resource requirement is 4N registers and 4Nm qubits; for a five-year auto loan example this becomes 240 registers and 1,920 qubits, exceeding near-term commercial hardware.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Quadratic sample-complexity improvement via QAE; resource scaling in the full competing-risks formulation is linear in N for registers and m for discretization, i.e. O(Nm) qubits in the best case described
